items.derivation: your venue is certified for 250 and you have 300 guests
items.mitigation: Compare the final RSVP against the written capacity; hold a 5–10 % buffer; name an overflow room.
items.title: Guest count exceeds certified capacity

items.mitigation: Walk every exit at 2 points in the day — at setup and again before doors; unlocked, unobstructed, opening outward; no storage in escape routes.
items.title: Blocked, locked or inward-opening exits

items.derivation: your plan has a dance floor and a stage
items.mitigation: Ask for floor loading figures; spread heavy items; cap raised staging at 4 people per m².
items.title: Floor load or collapse (dance floor, stage, bars)

items.mitigation: Rig only from certified points; request the rigging certificate and weight schedule 2 weeks before.
items.title: Ceiling rigging failure

items.mitigation: Dual supply; UPS on sound and AV; rehearse the changeover 2 times.
items.title: Power outage

items.derivation: you are running on a 100 kVA generator
items.mitigation: Size with 30–40 % headroom; fuel for the day plus 4 hours; a second smaller backup; service log.
items.title: Generator failure or fuel exhaustion

items.mitigation: Confirm the source and tank capacity; book a tanker backup on 24-hour call; separate potable storage for catering.
items.title: Water supply or tanker failure

items.mitigation: Shade on all seating; one water station per 50 guests; fans or misting; outdoor segments early or late; medical standby.
items.title: Heat

items.derivation: your event is in December, inside the harmattan
items.mitigation: Prefer indoor or covered; dust covers for cake and plated food; seal AV; warn guests 72 hours out about visibility, travel delays, dry eyes and respiratory effects.
items.title: Harmattan dust (Nov–Mar)

items.mitigation: Model the sun path at the actual ceremony hour and 2 hours either side; place the backdrop and shade accordingly.
items.title: Sun position and glare

items.mitigation: A 10 % RSVP buffer; overflow seating; a standing area; a second room.
items.title: Guest overflow

items.mitigation: A named list at the door, checked at 2 points; RSVP codes; a plus-one policy on the invite.
items.title: Uninvited guests, unearned plus-ones

items.mitigation: "Keep apart" tags on the chart; buffer tables by 1 m; a discreet re-seat plan.
items.title: Seating conflicts and family feuds

items.mitigation: A one-page protocol sheet; a named handler per VIP; reserved seating; arrival windows of 15 minutes.
items.title: VIP protocol

items.mitigation: A written setup window and venue access time; a 2-hour buffer before guest arrival.
items.title: Late vendors

items.mitigation: Confirmation calls at 7 and 2 days out; deposit-backed contracts; a backup contact per critical vendor.
items.title: No-shows

items.mitigation: A kids' area, activity packs, a planned early exit, one supervisor per 10 children.
items.title: Children

items.mitigation: A step-free route; one accessible toilet; 2 reserved seats per 50 guests; MC and sign-language provision.
items.title: Accessibility needs unmet

items.mitigation: One first-aider per 250 guests; the AED location; an ambulance access route; the nearest hospital printed.
items.title: Medical emergency

items.mitigation: One vetted guard per 100 guests; a guest list at the gate; a bag policy; a secure point for gifts and cash.
items.title: Security, theft or gatecrashing

items.mitigation: A guaranteed headcount plus 5–10 %; model plated against buffet; count vendor and crew meals.
items.title: Food runs out

items.mitigation: A backup PA; an offline playlist on two phones; a UPS; a sound check 2 hours before doors.
items.title: DJ or sound failure

items.mitigation: A backup-photographer clause; a second shooter; dual-card backup; confirm insurance 2 weeks out.
items.title: Photographer no-show or lost files

items.mitigation: Access time in writing; crew size specified; pre-build; a venue-ready deadline 2 hours before doors.
items.title: Decor setup delays

items.mitigation: A delivery window 4 hours before the cutting; refrigerated transport; an indoor display away from heat; a backup dessert.
items.title: Cake delivery failure or melt

items.mitigation: A confirmed fleet with driver contacts; one spare vehicle; departures staggered 15 minutes apart; a return schedule.
items.title: Transport or shuttle failure

items.mitigation: Pay by card; staged payments, no more than 50 % before the event; verify registration; event insurance covering supplier failure.
items.title: Deposit loss or vendor insolvency

items.mitigation: An itemised quote; an all-in comparison of 3 quotes; overtime and power rates in writing.
items.title: Hidden fees (service, corkage, overtime, power)

items.mitigation: A cancellation clause with a refund schedule; a tight force-majeure; a backup list of 2 vendors per category.
items.title: Vendor cancellation

items.mitigation: Lock prices at booking; pay early; cap adjustment clauses; a 10 % contingency.
items.title: Currency and inflation

items.mitigation: A run sheet with a 10-minute buffer between segments; hard stops; the MC has written authority to cut.
items.title: Schedule overrun

items.mitigation: Scripted transitions; 2 filler segments ready; an MC brief with names and pronunciations.
items.title: MC gaps and dead air

items.mitigation: A 5-minute limit per speaker; a speaker briefing; cue cards with a countdown.
items.title: Speeches overrun

items.mitigation: Tie service calls to the run sheet, 15 minutes before each course, not the caterer's convenience.
items.title: Food service timing fails

items.derivation: your plan has a stage for a band
items.mitigation: A dedicated 32 A circuit; a load calculation; a sound check at full load.
items.title: Power for the band

items.mitigation: Confirm in writing; a sound taper over the last 30 minutes; an indoor option; notify neighbours.
items.title: Noise curfew

items.mitigation: A venue fire risk assessment; extinguisher count; one trained marshal per 100 guests; an MC briefing line.
items.title: Fire safety gaps

items.mitigation: Venue public liability; vendor PL certificates for all suppliers; an event policy for cancellation and supplier failure, checked 6 weeks out.
items.title: Insurance gaps

notes: Likelihood and impact are practitioner judgement, not actuarial. They rank what to look at first; they do not predict what will happen.
Safety-critical risks are marked apart from experiential ones: a blocked exit and a late cake are not the same kind of problem.
Where the research gives no figure, the number in a mitigation is a planning heuristic, not a standard. Treat it as a starting point and adjust it to the venue.
